name: Royal Match
summary: Royal Match is a match-three puzzle game structured around one activity that pays into everything else: clearing a level. The level's star pays for building out a castle and its surrounding areas, its coins fund undoing failure and buying items, and every timed event running at once, a team tournament, a seasonal pass, a card collection, advances from the same completed level. Failure, not entry, is the switch that turns the loop into a monetization surface: hearts are only spent when a level is lost, and the paid offers are priced against exactly that shortfall.
teaser: Royal Match pays every part of itself, the castle, the team, the season, from the same completed level.

observations.name: Tracking permission comes first
observations.observed: Royal Match opens in vertical orientation and, before anything else, asks whether it can track the user's activity across other companies' apps and websites.
detail: The request precedes any gameplay, any account step and any explanation of the game.
No notification permission is requested at this point.

observations.name: Agreeing to the privacy policy
observations.observed: After the tracking request, Royal Match requires the user to agree to its privacy policy as a required step rather than an optional one.
detail: No account creation, sign-in or identity check is required before play begins.

observations.name: A guided first match
observations.observed: Royal Match places the user straight into gameplay, teaching the match-three action on the board itself by tying the instruction to a specific object rather than describing the goal in the abstract. As soon as the first match completes, the app marks the lesson finished.
detail: There's no pre-play tutorial screen, video or statement of the game's overall goal.
The instruction is tied to a specific board object rather than described in the abstract.

observations.name: Pointing out the task list
observations.observed: After the first lesson, Royal Match prompts the user that a task list exists and shows where to find it.

observations.name: The first castle-building task
observations.observed: Royal Match prompts the user to build a castle, shows area progress at the moment of that first build, and states the whole process runs six steps. The first step costs one star, which the user already holds, so the castle's first piece appears without any play required first.
detail: The area progress indicator appears at the moment of the first build rather than before it.
The result is described as a castle in a fairy-tale style.

observations.name: The star shortage names its own fix
observations.observed: The next task, a fountain, costs one star, and tapping it while short produces a message stating the user doesn't have enough stars, along with the route to get more: beat levels to earn them.
detail: The block is a resource shortage rather than a level or feature lock.
The earning route is stated only once the shortage is actually hit, not in advance.

observations.name: Locked boosters at level two
observations.observed: At level two, Royal Match states the goal as collecting 36 wooden pieces and shows a full set of boosters, all locked and unselectable.
detail: Their existence is disclosed before access to them is.
The level can be started immediately without the user making any choice at this screen.
No explanation of what the boosters do is given yet.

observations.name: Building continues, costs rise
observations.observed: After the second level, Royal Match prompts the user to keep improving the castle, plays a short animation for the completed fountain, and issues the next task, gazebos, at a cost of two stars, double the cost of the first two tasks.
detail: Each completed build is followed immediately by the next task rather than by a return to the board.

observations.name: The first unguided home screen
observations.observed: After two levels and two builds, Royal Match shows the home screen with the castle and lets the user explore freely. The screen carries a default grey and white profile icon, three balances, a settings button, the current level and area, and a five-item navigation bar.
detail: The three balances shown are 2,093 gold coins, five hearts and a store of gold stars.
The current state is shown as level three, area one.
The five navigation items are a book with stars, a golden cup, a home button, a badge showing several people, and a set of cards.
The coin total is already present without the app ever having shown where those coins came from.

observations.name: A target and a move limit, no clock
observations.observed: Each level states what must be achieved and how many moves remain, with no timer anywhere on the screen. Reaching the target within the moves completes the level; running out of moves ends it as a failure.
detail: Completing a level pays one star.
A failed level can be started again.

tags.name: Challenge
tags.rationale: Each level is a bounded objective instance: Royal Match states the success condition, such as collecting 36 wooden pieces, bounds it with a move limit, and produces a different response for completion than for exhausting the moves (tier: directly observed). The King's Nightmare interludes are separate bounded instances with their own success conditions and their own move or time boundaries (tier: directly observed). Propeller Madness, the Egg Hunt and the team tournament are event-bounded instances with stated success conditions and stated remaining time (tier: directly observed).
tags.alternativeConsidered: treating the bonus levels at 20 and 40 as challenges as well. They are excluded here: they state no success condition, only a quantity to accumulate within the moves given, so no completed-or-not-completed result exists for the instance (O18). Minigame was also considered for the King's Nightmare interludes and does not apply, because they pay coins into the ordinary balance; the bounded objective inside each one is carried by this entry.
tags.role:
engagement, retention.

The level instance is the unit of activity the user repeats inside a session (O10, O11), and the event instances carry countdowns that set a deadline for coming back (O29, O30, O33, O64).

observations.name: The board's objective changes
observations.observed: What must be destroyed or collected changes from level to level: breaking a box, collecting 36 wooden pieces, destroying patches of grass, matching next to mailboxes to collect mail, and breaking royal eggs.
detail: Mailboxes aren't destroyed directly; each qualifying match nearby collects mail from them.
The hard level at 39 is built from three mailboxes.

observations.name: Difficulty rises, and failure arrives around level 18
observations.observed: Royal Match increases difficulty gradually enough that ten levels pass before any booster is used. The first failures start at level 18, level 19 is failed twice in a row, and the game becomes noticeably harder past level 21.
detail: Boosters are banked rather than spent before the first failure.

observations.name: Hearts fall on failure, return on a timer
observations.observed: Royal Match starts the user with five hearts, consumed only when a level is failed. A spent heart restores in roughly 24 to 25 minutes.
detail: The lives panel offers a 900-coin refill.
The panel also offers to request free lives, showing a total of zero held and pointing the user to ask teammates.
After joining a team, buying more lives becomes available in a way it wasn't clearly before.
Royal Match doesn't show what happens once every heart is spent.

tags.name: Lives
tags.rationale: Royal Match holds five discrete hearts, removes one when a level is failed, and the remaining count governs whether another attempt can start (tier: directly observed). Restoration is defined at 24 to 25 minutes per heart, with a 900-coin refill and teammate requests as alternatives (tier: directly observed). Consumption is tied to failure rather than to entry: levels are started freely and hearts are reported lost at the failures from level 18 onward (tier: strongly supported, no heart is observed being consumed on entry).
tags.alternativeConsidered: Energy, which would apply if a heart were consumed on starting a level rather than on failing it. The session separates them: levels are entered and re-entered without a heart being taken until a level is failed.
tags.role:
engagement, retention, monetization.

Hearts decide whether the next attempt can begin at all (O13), the regeneration timer sets when the user can come back (O63), and the refill price and the unlimited-hearts periods in the offers are what the app sells against the shortage (O14, O57).

observations.name: A paid way to keep a failed level going
observations.observed: The first time the user runs out of moves, Royal Match offers five more moves for 900 coins to keep the level going.
detail: Declining is available, and the level then counts as a failure and can be retried.
That continuation price matches the price of a heart refill exactly.
A level failure costing 900 coins to undo, against a whole bonus level yielding roughly 500 coins, makes coins hard to accumulate relative to that cost.

observations.name: Assist items unlock one at a time
observations.observed: Royal Match releases its assist items progressively, teaching each one at the level where it becomes usable.
detail: A royal hammer that clears any object unlocks with a quantity of three after six or seven games.
An arrow that clears a row unlocks after level 14.
A cannon that clears a column unlocks after level 16.
A jester's hat that shuffles the board unlocks after level 18, with five uses.
TNT appears as a reward from offers and the Easter Pass and as a starting item in bonus levels.
A propeller that clears a row or column is introduced by the Propeller Madness event.
Each item's quantity is displayed and falls as it's used.

tags.name: Boosters
tags.rationale: Royal Match holds each assist item as a counted quantity outside the level, observed as three royal hammers and five jester's hats, displays the count before and during play, applies one only when the user selects the item and then a target, and reduces the count on use (tier: directly observed). The observed items are the royal hammer, an arrow that clears a row, a cannon that clears a column, a jester's hat that shuffles the board, TNT and the propeller, each with a stated effect (tier: directly observed). Replenishment routes observed are area chests, event rewards, the Easter Pass, the Easter Treasures ladder and the shop (tier: directly observed). The offers also sell unlimited use for stated periods from one hour to 100 hours, which suspends the count while the items remain per-instance selections (tier: directly observed).
tags.alternativeConsidered: Spendable Credits and Tokens, which would apply if the items were exchanged from a balance at the moment of use. The session separates the two: the coins are the balance, and the items are counted holdings applied inside the level. Energy was also considered and does not apply, since nothing is consumed unless the user selects an item.
tags.role:
engagement, monetization.

The items are selected and spent inside levels, including one spent at level 36 to protect the Butler's Gift state (O16, O21), and time-limited unlimited booster periods are most of what the named treasure bundles and the team offers contain (O57, O58).

observations.name: Choosing boosters before a level
observations.observed: Royal Match presents a booster selection before each level starts; at level two this selection is present but entirely locked.
detail: Once items are unlocked, the selection can be skipped, or an item can be chosen and used during play.
At level 36 the user uses a power-up specifically to avoid failing and losing a separate ongoing state.

observations.name: King's Nightmare interludes
observations.observed: At intervals, the ordinary play button is replaced by King's Nightmare, offering a 50-coin reward for a short activity that can be played or skipped.
detail: Each instance runs its own objective: carrying water to a sprinkler in 20 moves, breaking all the boxes before time runs out, and getting water to a king who isn't visible, in 30 moves.
One instance is timed rather than move-limited; another carries a doubled-reward marker and hides its target.
Each completion ends with a thank-you, confetti and trumpets, and the button reverts to the numbered level afterward.
The interludes resemble the gameplay style shown in the game's own advertising.

observations.name: Bonus levels at 20 and 40
observations.observed: Level 20 is presented as a bonus level, framed around collecting as many coins as possible within 20 moves, starting with two TNTs already in hand. Level 40 runs the same way.
detail: Neither carries a pass or fail condition; the outcome is simply the quantity collected.
Matches next to coins collect them directly, and combining two TNTs pays an immediate 80 coins.
The bonus level pays more than 500 coins.
What the reward will be isn't stated beyond the coin framing before entry.

tags.name: Reward Multiplier
tags.rationale: Two stated modifiers are observed. At level 33 the app marks the level with a doubling marker, starts a 15-minute countdown and states that rewards are doubled for the duration; during the window the contribution paid to the team and the progress paid to Propeller Madness both move at twice their earlier rate (tier: directly observed). Level 39 is marked as a hard level before entry and states that passing it triples the reward and pays 30 points to the Egg Hunt (tier: directly observed). In both cases the base reward exists independently of the modifier and the factor is stated, so the modified amount follows from a visible rule (tier: directly observed). A third instance is the King's Nightmare interlude that carries a doubled-reward marker over its stated 50 coins (tier: directly observed).
tags.alternativeConsidered: Variable Reward Outcome, which would apply if the increased amount were unresolved before the reward event. Both instances state the factor in advance, which settles it. Boosters was also considered for the doubling marker and does not apply: nothing is held or expended, and the conditions of the level are unchanged.
tags.role:
engagement.

Both modifiers change what the level in front of the user pays without changing the level, and the fifteen-minute window is spent inside the session that opened it (O19, O22).

observations.name: The king reacts to the board
observations.observed: When few moves remain and objectives are still outstanding, Royal Match shows the king looking worried, appearing around three remaining moves with work still to do.
detail: On success, the king thanks the user with confetti.
The expression tracks the board's current state rather than being something the user selects or owns.

observations.name: Butler's Gift rewards first-try wins
observations.observed: Royal Match introduces Butler's Gift, stating "beat levels on your first try to start the next level with power-ups." The state is later shown active for two of the last three levels.
detail: At level 36 the user spends a power-up specifically to avoid failing and losing this state.
What happens to it after a level isn't cleared on the first try isn't shown.

tags.name: Streak
tags.rationale: Butler's Gift is framed by the app as "beat levels on your first try to start the next level with power-ups", and its state is displayed as active on two out of three, so the benefit depends on a run of first-try clearances rather than on a total count of them (tier: directly observed). The continuity rule itself, what a failure does to the state, was never observed, because the narrator spent a power-up specifically to avoid finding out (tier: directly observed). Under the presence standard the surface and the app's own framing establish the mechanic; the reset behavior is stated here as not observed.
tags.alternativeConsidered: a cumulative count of first-try wins within a bounded set of three levels, in which gaps would not matter. The profile's "first try wins" stat is exactly such a count and is not tagged here. What would separate them is observing a level that is not cleared on the first try and whether the two-out-of-three state falls back.
tags.role:
engagement.

The state is what makes the narrator spend a power-up to avoid failing a level he would otherwise have retried, which changes how the level in front of him is played (O16, O21).

detail: Both the contribution paid to the team and the progress paid to Propeller Madness move at twice their normal rate during the window.
What actually opens the window isn't stated; the user's first reaction is that its meaning is unknown, and the explanation only comes from opening it.

observations.name: Stars fund optional building
observations.observed: Royal Match prompts the user to spend held stars on the current area task each time enough are held, and the prompt can be dismissed; play continues and stars can simply accumulate. A marker appears next to the area chest whenever stars are held and a task is still waiting.
detail: Area-one tasks include the castle, the fountain, gazebos, bushes, swans and flowers across six steps.
Area two adds glass, carpet and chairs; area three is stated to hold nine things to customize.
Task costs rise from one star to two within area one.
Each build completes immediately once its cost is paid, with an animation.

observations.name: Finishing an area
observations.observed: Completing an area produces a chest to open, a celebration, a view of the finished area, and then a new area to unlock.
detail: The area-one chest pays 250 gold coins and four kinds of boosters and power-ups.
The area-two chest is reported as paying more than the previous one, without contents listed.
The area-three chest pays 250 coins, further items and four Culinary Collection cards.
Area one completes at level 11, area two at level 21, and area three shortly after level 41.
Each new area is presented as a separate step the user taps to unlock.

observations.name: Events run on ordinary level play
observations.observed: Once its events are running, Royal Match advances every one of them from the same match-three levels the user is already playing, rather than from any separate activity.
detail: Tournament tokens, Easter Pass keys, Egg Hunt eggs and Propeller Madness steps all move forward this way.
The Easter Pass states its instruction as beating levels and collecting keys, and the Egg Hunt states beating levels and collecting eggs.
A token moves into the team tournament after a completed level.
Royal Match doesn't state how much a given level contributes to any of these values.

tags.name: Experience Points
tags.rationale: Royal Match runs several quantified progression values that are granted for qualifying level play and accumulate toward stated thresholds: tournament tokens, which convert to lances and advance both a contributor state and the team's position; Easter Pass keys, which advance ordered positions on the pass; Egg Hunt eggs, which advance toward the next basket; and the propellers and then collected coins that advance the Propeller Madness steps (tier: directly observed). None of them is exchangeable for a user-selected result, which separates them from the spendable balances (tier: strongly supported, no spending route is shown for any of them). The confidence is strongly supported rather than directly observed because the grant rule, how much each level contributes to each measure, is never stated and the narrator asks for it without an answer (tier: directly observed, at O25).
tags.alternativeConsidered: Spendable Credits and Tokens, which would apply if the tokens, keys or eggs could be exchanged for a chosen result. The one unit that does behave that way, the card star used to open chests, is treated separately and is recorded under the unresolved list. What would separate them for the others is observing any surface where a token, key or egg is spent by choice.
tags.role:
engagement, retention.

The event units are what makes an ordinary level worth playing now rather than later (O25, O42), and each one is attached to a countdown that sets when the accumulation has to happen (O64).

observations.name: The player level as running state
observations.observed: Royal Match keeps a current level for the user, shows it on the home screen, advances it by one for each level cleared, and uses it as the condition for other parts of the product. Play moves from level one past level 41 by the account's current point.
detail: Other players' levels are shown on the leaderboards, with the highest shown at 13,401.
Level is the stated condition for both joining teams and reaching the collection.

tags.name: Leveling
tags.rationale: Royal Match assigns the user a current level within an ordered series, advances it by one for each level cleared, displays it on the home screen and on the leaderboards, and uses it as the condition for other parts of the product (tier: directly observed). The ordered series extends far beyond the session: the highest level observed on the world leaderboard is 13,401 (tier: directly observed). The tournament also maintains an ordered contributor state, observed as an armour colour changing from silver to gold and a knight title at a stated token threshold (tier: directly observed).
tags.alternativeConsidered: treating the numbered levels only as content units rather than as a progression state. That is ruled out because the app maintains and displays the number as the user's current state and gates other features on it. The conditions placed on those features are not classified here; this entry covers the measure and Progression Gate covers the conditions read from it.
tags.role:
engagement, retention.

The level is what advances each time the user plays a level (O10, O26), and the features it releases, teams at 21 and the collection at 41, are what the user is still playing toward across sessions (O34, O35).

observations.name: An area map of 152

detail: The user starts outside the map and scrolls upward through what remains.
Area names shown in order are area one, the throne room, the dining room and the garden.

observations.name: The profile's running stats
observations.observed: The profile shows the user's level, team membership and join date, alongside a set of running counts: first-try wins, helps received, areas completed, collections completed and sets completed.
detail: These are presented as counts rather than as attained states or badges.

Each following step opens a further one with a better reward, ending in the grand prize.
Rewards from steps already passed can be collected while the event runs.
The propeller is itself a board item that erases a row or a column.

Tapping play on the event pop-up leads into the next ordinary level rather than a separate mode.

observations.name: The Easter Pass, a two-lane track
observations.observed: At level 37, Royal Match introduces the Easter Pass with a 27-day 12-hour countdown and a first reward ready to claim, instructing the user to beat levels and collect keys to unlock rewards.
detail: A second, purchasable lane pays more at the same 30 positions as the free lane.
The first position pays one TNT free; the paid lane instead pays eight lives, a golden frame, a golden username and a teammate gift.
The second position pays one coloured candy free, or 15 minutes of infinite hearts paid.
The final position pays triple power-ups and boosters free, or an hour of unlimited boosters plus 1,000 coins paid.
A bonus reward sits at the very bottom of the track, unlocked by activating the pass, and nothing about it is shown anywhere before the user scrolls all the way down to find it.
The pass is also offered from the bottom of the lives panel.

tags.name: Seasonal Progression Pass
tags.rationale: The Easter Pass is a bounded track: it carries a 27-day 12-hour countdown, holds 30 ordered positions, is advanced by beating levels and collecting keys, and pays a reward at each reached position (tier: directly observed). A second lane at the same positions is unlocked by a purchase and pays more at each, along with exclusive items stated to last until the event ends (tier: directly observed). The seasonal boundary is what selects this entry over Progression Fund.
tags.alternativeConsidered: Progression Fund, which covers an unbounded track attached to a measure the product already maintains. Both are excluded here: the pass carries an event boundary that ends it, and it runs on keys of its own rather than on the player level. Season Content Pass was also considered and does not apply, since the entitlement pays rewards at positions rather than granting access to grouped content.
tags.role:
monetization, retention, engagement.

The activated lane is sold for a stated price at the moment the track appears (O60), the 27-day window and the marker on the key icon are what bring the user back to claim (O31, O66), and the keys that advance it come from ordinary play (O25).

observations.name: The Culinary Collection begins
observations.observed: After level 40, Royal Match starts the Culinary Collection, framed around completing sets for rewards, running 27 days and 12 hours, and grants a first pack of four cards.
detail: The collection holds 15 sets of nine cards each, 135 in total.
The first pack yields a rolling pin, falafel, marshmallow and sorbet.
The named sets include frozen, street foods, sweets, garnishes, tools, dairy, pastries, spices, cuisines, snacks, market, coffee, drinks, dining and breakfast.
Cards come from packs, chests and teammates; duplicates convert into card stars, which the app states are used to open further chests.
The grand prize for completing every set is 10,000 coins, a chef badge and ten times boosters.
Completing area three grants four further cards.

tags.name: Set Collection
tags.rationale: The Culinary Collection defines 15 named sets of nine cards each, tracks which cards are held, states the reward for completing each set and a grand prize for completing all of them, and treats a repeat card differently from a new one by converting duplicates into card stars (tier: directly observed). Cards arrive from packs, chests and teammates (tier: directly observed).
tags.alternativeConsidered: treating the card stars as the collectible rather than the cards. That is ruled out: the sets track named cards at member level, and the stars are what duplicates become.
tags.role:
engagement, social, retention.

Completing sets is what the cards are for and what the card requests to teammates serve (O32, O51), and the collection's 27-day window is what dates the work (O64).

observations.name: The team tournament ranks contribution
observations.observed: After joining a team with enough members, Royal Match shows a team tournament, framed as converting tokens into lances contributed to the team. The surface shows the team's current position, the reward at the next position, each member's contribution, and the user's own standing inside the team.
detail: The team sits at position nine at one point, with four more tokens needed for the next reward, a power-up.
Members with zero contribution are marked as earning nothing.
After level 26 the user needs 76 more tokens to become a knight.
After level 34 the user's armour changes from silver to gold, shown in second place within the team.
The tournament runs on a countdown of two days and 13 hours.
What a lance is actually worth in tokens isn't stated.

tags.name: Challenge
tags.rationale: Each level is a bounded objective instance: Royal Match states the success condition, such as collecting 36 wooden pieces, bounds it with a move limit, and produces a different response for completion than for exhausting the moves (tier: directly observed). The King's Nightmare interludes are separate bounded instances with their own success conditions and their own move or time boundaries (tier: directly observed). Propeller Madness, the Egg Hunt and the team tournament are event-bounded instances with stated success conditions and stated remaining time (tier: directly observed).
tags.alternativeConsidered: treating the bonus levels at 20 and 40 as challenges as well. They are excluded here: they state no success condition, only a quantity to accumulate within the moves given, so no completed-or-not-completed result exists for the instance (O18). Minigame was also considered for the King's Nightmare interludes and does not apply, because they pay coins into the ordinary balance; the bounded objective inside each one is carried by this entry.
tags.role:
engagement, retention.

The level instance is the unit of activity the user repeats inside a session (O10, O11), and the event instances carry countdowns that set a deadline for coming back (O29, O30, O33, O64).

tags.name: Leveling
tags.rationale: Royal Match assigns the user a current level within an ordered series, advances it by one for each level cleared, displays it on the home screen and on the leaderboards, and uses it as the condition for other parts of the product (tier: directly observed). The ordered series extends far beyond the session: the highest level observed on the world leaderboard is 13,401 (tier: directly observed). The tournament also maintains an ordered contributor state, observed as an armour colour changing from silver to gold and a knight title at a stated token threshold (tier: directly observed).
tags.alternativeConsidered: treating the numbered levels only as content units rather than as a progression state. That is ruled out because the app maintains and displays the number as the user's current state and gates other features on it. The conditions placed on those features are not classified here; this entry covers the measure and Progression Gate covers the conditions read from it.
tags.role:
engagement, retention.

The level is what advances each time the user plays a level (O10, O26), and the features it releases, teams at 21 and the collection at 41, are what the user is still playing toward across sessions (O34, O35).

tags.name: Milestone
tags.rationale: Royal Match maintains a broader progression, 152 areas and an open-ended level count, and recognizes defined points within it separately from ordinary progress. Completing an area produces a chest, a celebration, a view of the finished area and the unlock of the next one (tier: directly observed). Levels 20 and 40 are both presented as bonus levels, marking a recognized point at every twentieth level (tier: strongly supported, two instances 20 apart are observed and the pattern is stated by the narration rather than by the app). The tournament states a knight title at a token threshold, a defined point within the token progression (tier: directly observed).
tags.alternativeConsidered: Achievement for area completion. It is not applied because the app records a count of areas completed rather than a preserved attained state for each area, and the area unlock follows automatically from the progression rather than recording a separate accomplishment. Progression Gate was also considered for the area unlocks and does not apply: the next area is the next unit of the area progression rather than a separate part of the product withheld against a stated value.
tags.role:
engagement, retention.

Area completion is the point the castle work is aimed at and the moment a new area opens (O23, O24), and the bonus level at every twentieth level marks a recognized point in the level run (O18).

tags.name: Clan / Guild
tags.rationale: Royal Match represents the team as a collective entity with its own badge, name, description, roster, capacity of 50, joining requirement and, decisively, its own group-level state: a team score, a position in the tournament standings, and tournament rewards earned at the team level (tier: directly observed). Member activity feeds that collective state through contributed lances (tier: directly observed). Membership changes observable conditions: free lives, the tournament, card requests and the team message board (tier: directly observed). Under the decision ladder for the three sibling social entries, the presence of a collective group-owned state selects this entry.
tags.alternativeConsidered: Group Membership and Community Space, its two sibling entries. Both are excluded by the decision ladder: the team holds collective state of its own, which is the more specific distinguishing feature, so the single label for this surface is this entry.
tags.role:
social, retention, monetization.

The team is where other identified players appear, send lives and cards, and stand in a shared ranking (O47, O49, O50, O51), the waiting requests are a reason to come back (O66), and the team offers turn the roster into the thing being sold to (O58).

tags.name: Leaderboard
tags.rationale: Royal Match presents ordered lists of comparable entities in several scopes: players by level and crowns for the world and for the user's country, teams by team score for the world and for the country, and, inside the tournament, teams by position and members by contribution (tier: directly observed). Each list shows at least two entities in relative order with the comparison value displayed (tier: directly observed).
tags.alternativeConsidered: Comparative Rank alone. Both are applied, because the ordered lists and the user's own communicated position are distinct co-occurring behaviors rather than one behavior carved two ways.
tags.role:
social, engagement.

The lists are populated by other identified players and teams with names and pictures (O46, O47), and the tournament standing with its per-member contribution column is what the contribution prompt points at (O33, O52).

tags.name: Comparative Rank
tags.rationale: Royal Match communicates positions that depend on other entities' results: the team is at position nine, the team is reported moving between positions eight and nine without the user's own contribution changing, and the user is shown in second place inside the team with an armour colour that changes as the standing improves (tier: directly observed). The tournament scope is bounded by the event window (tier: directly observed).
tags.alternativeConsidered: a progression tier, which would apply if the armour colour were reached from fixed thresholds rather than from standing against the other members. The surface states a position, second place, alongside the colour change, which settles it for the tournament; the knight title at a stated token threshold is treated separately under Milestone.
tags.role:
social, engagement.

The position the app tells the user about is their team's place among other teams and their own place among named teammates, and it is stated next to the reward that position earns (O33, O52).

observations.name: Teams require level 21
observations.observed: The teams navigation item states that level 21 is required to join a team. A team can be viewed before then, but tapping join produces the same requirement message.
detail: No request can be sent while under level 21.
The stated value of joining is free lives and free rewards.
The prompt to join arrives on completing level 20, one level before it can be acted on.
The top team requires level 13,400 and is marked closed with high activity; some teams also state a crown requirement.

tags.name: Progression Gate
tags.rationale: Royal Match maintains the player level as a measure it advances through the user's own play, one level per cleared level (tier: directly observed). Three parts of the product are withheld against stated values of that measure: teams at level 21, the collection at level 41, and each assist item at its own level (tier: directly observed). Each requirement is stated in the terms of the measure and is observable before it is satisfied: the teams surface can be browsed and repeats "reach level 21 to join teams" when join is tapped, the collection tab states level 41 and describes nothing else, and locked items are displayed but cannot be tapped (tier: directly observed). Each withheld part is distinct from the level progression itself rather than being the next level in it (tier: directly observed).
tags.alternativeConsidered: Milestone, which covers the product's recognition that a defined point in a progression has been reached. It is not applied to these three, because a gate is the standing condition on a withheld part rather than the recognition event at the crossing. The team tournament's requirement of at least ten members was also considered and is excluded: roster size is not a measure the user advances by playing, so it is an eligibility condition and is recorded in plain language at O37.
tags.role:
retention, engagement.

The two feature gates state a level the user does not hold and can reach only by playing more across sessions (O34, O35), and the item gates release the level's own tools one at a time between levels 8 and 18, which changes what each level can be played with (O36).

observations.name: The collection requires level 41
observations.observed: The last navigation item states that level 41 is required to unlock the collection and gives no description of what the collection actually is.
detail: The Culinary Collection itself begins once level 40 is completed.

observations.name: Assist items are gated by level
observations.observed: Royal Match locks its boosters and power-ups at the start and releases them at specific levels: the royal hammer after six or seven games, the arrow after level 14, the cannon after level 16, and the jester's hat after level 18.
detail: Locked items are shown but can't be tapped.
Each unlock is followed by a short instruction at the level where it first becomes usable.

observations.name: Ten members required for the tournament
observations.observed: After level 22, Royal Match shows a team tournament pop-up along with a notice that at least ten members are needed to participate, which the user's current team doesn't have.
detail: The user leaves that team and joins one that meets the requirement, at which point the tournament appears.
Leaving a team asks for confirmation.
Only one team can be held at a time.

observations.name: Two closed surfaces: Royal League and friends
observations.observed: At the top of the areas surface, Royal Match shows Royal League, and tapping it does nothing; Royal Match gives no explanation of it anywhere.
detail: The friends tab of the leaderboard shows only a prompt to connect with Facebook, and the friends list can't be reached without that connection.
Declining the connection produces a sign-in failure message.

observations.name: Gold coins, earned and spent widely
observations.observed: Royal Match grants gold coins from level play, King's Nightmare interludes, bonus levels, area chests and event rewards, holding them as a balance shown on the home screen. Coins are spent on a 900-coin heart refill and 900 coins for five extra moves, and are also sold in packs for money.
detail: The balance stands at 2,093 after two levels.
The King's Nightmare reward is 50 coins, later doubled.
An area chest pays 250; a bonus level pays over 500; event grand prizes are stated at 10,000.
On first seeing the shop, what coins are actually for isn't yet clear to the user.
No spending route other than lives, moves and offer-granted items appears.

tags.name: Soft Currency
tags.rationale: Royal Match maintains two earned balances that are deliberately spent for product-defined results. Gold coins are granted by level play, interludes, bonus levels, chests and event rewards, and are spent on a heart refill at 900 and on five extra moves at 900 (tier: directly observed). Gold stars are granted at one per cleared level and are spent on area tasks costing one or two stars (tier: directly observed). Both remain stored until spent and both reduce on the exchange (tier: directly observed). This entry is a specialization of Spendable Credits and Tokens, whose invariant it preserves while adding the repeatable non-paid acquisition path.
tags.alternativeConsidered: Experience Points for gold stars, which would apply if stars accumulated toward an advancement threshold rather than being exchanged. The session settles it: stars are deliberately spent on a chosen task and the balance falls when they are.
tags.role:
engagement, monetization.

Stars are what the user plays levels to obtain and spends on the castle inside a session (O23, O40), and the coin balance is the thing the shop's whole price ladder is built to sell (O39, O56).

tags.name: Hard Currency
tags.rationale: The same gold coin balance that is earned in play is sold for money in fixed packs, observed from 1,000 coins at 1.99 up to 100,000 coins at 99.99, and is also included in every named treasure bundle (tier: directly observed). The purchased units enter the stored balance rather than delivering a final result, and are later exchanged for refills, moves and offer items (tier: directly observed). Where one balance carries both a paid and an earned path, this entry still applies alongside Soft Currency; both are specializations of Spendable Credits and Tokens.
tags.alternativeConsidered: classifying the coin packs as direct purchases of the underlying benefit. That is ruled out because payment adds to a stored balance that the user allocates later, rather than granting the refill or the moves themselves.
tags.role:
monetization, engagement.

Money enters the game as coins rather than as the thing the user wants, and the coins then pay for the refill and the extra moves that keep a failed attempt going (O14, O39, O56).

observations.name: Gold stars, one faucet and one sink
observations.observed: Royal Match grants one gold star for each level cleared and accepts stars only as payment for area-building tasks. Holding too few stars blocks a task, and the app states that levels must be beaten to earn more.
detail: Task costs are one and two stars.
Stars accumulate if the user doesn't build.
Because one level pays one star, a two-star task takes two levels to afford, which is where building visibly slows relative to level clears.
No route to stars other than clearing levels appears.

observations.name: Hearts, bounded and restored three ways
observations.observed: Royal Match holds hearts as a balance bounded at five, consumed on failure, restored on a timer, purchasable with coins, or obtainable from teammates.
detail: The Easter Pass raises this bound to eight while active.
Paid offers grant periods of unlimited hearts, from 15 minutes up to 18 hours, rather than heart quantities.
The lives panel routes the user to teammates whenever no free lives are held.

tags.name: Lives
tags.rationale: Royal Match holds five discrete hearts, removes one when a level is failed, and the remaining count governs whether another attempt can start (tier: directly observed). Restoration is defined at 24 to 25 minutes per heart, with a 900-coin refill and teammate requests as alternatives (tier: directly observed). Consumption is tied to failure rather than to entry: levels are started freely and hearts are reported lost at the failures from level 18 onward (tier: strongly supported, no heart is observed being consumed on entry).
tags.alternativeConsidered: Energy, which would apply if a heart were consumed on starting a level rather than on failing it. The session separates them: levels are entered and re-entered without a heart being taken until a level is failed.
tags.role:
engagement, retention, monetization.

Hearts decide whether the next attempt can begin at all (O13), the regeneration timer sets when the user can come back (O63), and the refill price and the unlimited-hearts periods in the offers are what the app sells against the shortage (O14, O57).

observations.name: Event units: tokens, keys, eggs, propellers and card stars
observations.observed: Royal Match runs several separate counted units, each belonging to one event and each advanced by ordinary level play: tokens that convert to lances for the team, keys that advance the Easter Pass, eggs that advance the Egg Hunt, propellers and then coins that advance Propeller Madness, and duplicate cards that become card stars.
detail: None of these is spendable on a user-chosen purchase except card stars, which the collection states are used to open chests.
Each is shown as progress toward a stated next threshold rather than as a free balance.
The rate any of them is granted per level isn't stated.

tags.name: Experience Points
tags.rationale: Royal Match runs several quantified progression values that are granted for qualifying level play and accumulate toward stated thresholds: tournament tokens, which convert to lances and advance both a contributor state and the team's position; Easter Pass keys, which advance ordered positions on the pass; Egg Hunt eggs, which advance toward the next basket; and the propellers and then collected coins that advance the Propeller Madness steps (tier: directly observed). None of them is exchangeable for a user-selected result, which separates them from the spendable balances (tier: strongly supported, no spending route is shown for any of them). The confidence is strongly supported rather than directly observed because the grant rule, how much each level contributes to each measure, is never stated and the narrator asks for it without an answer (tier: directly observed, at O25).
tags.alternativeConsidered: Spendable Credits and Tokens, which would apply if the tokens, keys or eggs could be exchanged for a chosen result. The one unit that does behave that way, the card star used to open chests, is treated separately and is recorded under the unresolved list. What would separate them for the others is observing any surface where a token, key or egg is spent by choice.
tags.role:
engagement, retention.

The event units are what makes an ordinary level worth playing now rather than later (O25, O42), and each one is attached to a countdown that sets when the accumulation has to happen (O64).

observations.name: Crowns and team score, unexplained
observations.observed: The players leaderboard shows crowns beside other players, with values as high as 11,000, and some teams state crowns are needed to join.
detail: Teams also carry a team score, the highest reported as roughly 700 million.
Royal Match doesn't state what crowns are, and shows no route to earning or spending them.
Team capacity is shown as up to 50 members.

observations.name: Chests and packs, variable contents
observations.observed: Royal Match grants chests on area completion and card packs in the Culinary Collection, with contents that differ between openings.
detail: The area-one chest pays 250 coins and four kinds of boosters and power-ups.
The area-three chest pays 250 coins, further items and four cards.
The first card pack pays four named cards and a later pack pays four different ones.
Contents aren't disclosed before opening, which is presented as a separate tap with a reveal.
The collection states that duplicate card stars can open further chests, though Royal Match doesn't show whether those particular chests vary in contents.

tags.name: Variable Reward Outcome
tags.rationale: Royal Match grants chests and card packs whose contents are not disclosed before opening and which resolve to materially different results between instances: the area-one chest yields 250 coins and four kinds of items, the area-three chest yields 250 coins, items and four cards, and successive card packs yield different named cards (tier: directly observed). Opening is a separate action with a reveal (tier: directly observed). No value is committed to obtain these particular containers, which is what keeps them under this entry rather than under its specialization, Loot Box.
tags.alternativeConsidered: Loot Box, its specialization, which requires a value commitment made before the contents are known. The free chests and packs carry no such commitment. The card-star chests do, and they are recorded as unresolved rather than tagged here. The doubled and tripled reward amounts at O22 and O19 are not this entry either: they follow from a stated factor, which places them under Reward Multiplier.
tags.role:
engagement, retention.

The chests and card packs are the payoff at the end of each area and each event step, and what is inside is the reason to open them rather than a stated amount the user already knows (O24, O32, O44).

observations.name: Setting an identity, unprompted
observations.observed: Tapping the profile image lets the user set a username, use a Facebook photo or choose an avatar, pick a frame, and choose a display name. Royal Match never prompts the user to do any of this; the default is a plain grey and white silhouette until the user finds these options on their own.
detail: Once set, the chosen name and frame show on the profile.
The Easter Pass's paid lane sells a golden frame and golden username at the first position of its activated track.

tags.name: Cosmetic Customization
tags.rationale: Royal Match maintains selectable presentation states for the user's identity: an avatar or a Facebook photo, a frame, and a chosen name, none of which changes any rule, cost or outcome (tier: directly observed). The activated Easter Pass lane replaces these with a golden profile picture frame and a golden username for the duration of the event (tier: directly observed).
tags.alternativeConsidered: the castle and area decorations, which are the most visible presentation change in the game. They are not tagged here: the built state is the direct visible consequence of spending stars on the current task, no alternative presentation is offered for any task, and the appearance cannot be applied independently of that progression state. The star sink is described in plain language at O23 and O40 instead.
tags.role:
social, monetization.

The avatar, frame and name are what other identified players see beside the user on the leaderboards and in the team (O46, O47), and the golden frame and golden username are sold as part of the pass activation (O60).

detail: The highest level on the world list is 13,401, with crowns as high as 11,000.
The country list shows a comparable set of players at the same top level.
The user's own position within either list is not shown.

detail: Some teams can be joined directly; others require a sent request.
The prompt to join arrives right after level 20, stating free lives and free rewards as the value of joining.
The user holds only one team membership at a time, leaving one team, with a confirmation step, before joining another.

The team is where other identified players appear, send lives and cards, and stand in a shared ranking (O47, O49, O50, O51), the waiting requests are a reason to come back (O66), and the team offers turn the roster into the thing being sold to (O58).

observations.name: The team message board
observations.observed: Inside a team, Royal Match shows a shared message board carrying messages and help requests from members, including one life request timestamped well over two years earlier alongside current ones.
detail: The user can type and send a message to the team directly, which appears there once sent.
Requests and messages are associated with the team rather than a private conversation.

observations.name: Sending and requesting lives
observations.observed: A teammate's request for a life can be answered directly; doing so sends a life and pays the sender five coins.
detail: Answering the same request a second time is blocked with a message stating it's already been helped.
The user can also send a request of their own, stated to last four hours.
The lives panel routes an empty personal supply of free lives straight to this same teammate-request route.

tags.name: Gifting
tags.rationale: The user sends a life to an identified teammate in response to that teammate's request, the recipient receives it without returning anything, and the app blocks a second help on the same request with "you already helped" (tier: directly observed). The sender receives five coins for the transfer (tier: directly observed). The purchased team offers direct a period of infinite hearts to every member of the roster, and the activated Easter Pass lane includes a gift for teammates (tier: directly observed).
tags.alternativeConsidered: treating the card requests as gifting. They are recorded as a request route here rather than tagged, because the session shows the request being sent and never shows a card being directed to a recipient.

A life is directed to an identified teammate who asked for it and the sender is paid five coins for doing so (O50), the received life is what lets the recipient keep playing (O13), and the same gifting route is what the paid team offers and the activated pass lane sell (O58, O60).

observations.name: Requesting cards from teammates
observations.observed: Once the Culinary Collection is running, the team surface lets the user request a specific card from teammates, choosing one card at a time.
detail: A sent card request is stated to last 24 hours, longer than the four-hour window on a life request.
The team icon carries a numbered marker whenever a teammate's own request is waiting to be answered.
The collection names friends as one source of cards alongside packs and chests.

observations.name: Contribution as the price of the team reward
observations.observed: The team tournament states plainly that members who don't contribute receive no reward, and shows each member's individual contribution next to the team's overall position.
detail: The Easter Pass's activated lane includes a gift specifically for teammates.
The purchased team offers grant every member of the roster a period of unlimited hearts rather than rewarding only the buyer.

The sender receives five coins for the transfer (tier: directly observed). The purchased team offers direct a period of infinite hearts to every member of the roster, and the activated Easter Pass lane includes a gift for teammates (tier: directly observed).
